hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes this only because it is an instance-implicit section variable and `σ` is an argument. Nothing in the statement needs it. `varIdeal R σ` is defined as `Ideal.span (Set.range MvPolynomial.X)`, with only `[CommRing R]`. `Finsupp.degree` and `MvPolynomial.coeff` also need no decidability on σ. The proof uses it only through `lowVanish R σ N` (which takes `[DecidableEq σ]`) inside `varIdeal_pow_le_lowVanish`. Without the binder, the proof can start with `classical` and apply the same lemma: membership in `lowVanish` unfolds to the decidability-free condition `∀ d, d.degree < N → coeff d p = 0` (`mem_lowVanish` is `Iff.rfl`), so the conclusion is unchanged. There are no degenerate cases, since the statement does not depend on this instance at all.

It is pulled in as an instance-implicit section variable. Note that `mem_lowVanish` right above it even has `omit [Fintype σ] in`. The statement is true for any σ, finite or not. Every element of `(span (range X))^N` is a combination of products of N variables times polynomials, so every monomial in its support has degree ≥ N. The current proof uses finiteness only in `varIdeal_pow_le_lowVanish`, where `Ideal.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun` (which requires `Fintype`) writes q ∈ span(range X) as a finite sum ∑ c s * X s. Without finiteness, the same induction on N works if that step is replaced by `Submodule.span_induction` on q ∈ span(range X), proving p * q ∈ lowVanish (N+1) for p ∈ lowVanish N. The zero, addition and scalar cases hold because `lowVanish (N+1)` is an ideal (p * (a * q) = a * (p * q)). The generator case q = X s is exactly the existing `coeff_mul_X'` computation. With σ empty, varIdeal is ⊥ and every d has degree 0; for N = 0 the hypothesis `d.degree < 0` is false, and for N ≥ 1, p = 0. So the statement still holds there. The two binders can also both be deleted together.
